title: Decode a Modbus RTU Read Response
statement:
Decode a Modbus RTU reply from a grid meter, and refuse it unless every check passes.

A meter reports active power as a **signed 32-bit value in two 16-bit holding registers**. You asked for both registers with function `0x03`. The reply is one frame of bytes.

## The frame

A good reply is **9 bytes**:

```
addr  func  bytecount  r1hi r1lo r2hi r2lo  crc_lo crc_hi
 0     1       2        3    4    5    6      7      8
```

- `func` is `0x03`, `bytecount` is `4`.
- The value is `r1` then `r2`, **high word first**, as a signed 32-bit number, big-endian.
- The CRC is **CRC-16/MODBUS**: polynomial `0xA001` (reflected), initial value `0xFFFF`, no final XOR. It covers every byte before it. It is sent **low byte first**.

An **exception reply** is shorter: `addr, func|0x80, code, crc_lo, crc_hi` (5 bytes).

## Your function

```
int modbus_read_response(const uint8_t *frame, size_t len,
                         uint8_t expected_addr, int32_t *value_out);
```

Run the checks **in this order** and return the first code that applies. Write `*value_out` only on success.

| Order | Check | Return |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `len < 5` | `-1` |
| 2 | CRC over `frame[0 .. len-3]` does not match the last two bytes | `-2` |
| 3 | `frame[0] != expected_addr` | `-3` |
| 4 | `frame[1]` has bit `0x80` set (exception reply) | `-4` |
| 5 | `frame[1] != 0x03` | `-5` |
| 6 | `len != 9` or `frame[2] != 4` | `-6` |
| | all good | `0` |

The harness prints `OK <value>` or `ERR <code>`. Each input line is the expected address, then the frame bytes, all in hex.

## Watch out

- Check the length **before** you read the CRC bytes.
- Do not read `frame[3]` onwards until step 6 has passed. A 5-byte exception frame has no data bytes.
- The value is signed. A raw `0xFFFFFFFB` is `-5`.

tests.name: a negative value
tests.description: The raw value is 0xFFFFFBxx: sign matters.

tests.name: the wrong slave address
tests.description: The CRC is fine. The address is not the one we asked.

tests.name: an exception reply
tests.description: Five bytes, bit 0x80 set. There are no data bytes to read.
